title: Homomorphisms of connected affine groups are determined by restriction to a Borel
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G,H$ be smooth connected affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $B\subseteq G$ be a Borel subgroup [def-sfb-borel-subgroup-scheme], a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. For any commutative $k$-algebra $R$, write $G_R=G\times_k\operatorname{Spec}R$, and likewise for $H_R$ and $B_R$; these are the scalar extensions of the group schemes [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If $f_1,f_2:G_R\to H_R$ are homomorphisms of $R$-group schemes and their restrictions to $B_R$ agree as scheme morphisms, then $f_1=f_2$ as morphisms of $R$-group schemes. The algebra $R$ need not be reduced, and no reductivity or characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, printed p.358, including its arbitrary k-algebra R clause; Section 17b, printed p.353, for the connected group-variety and algebraically closed base conventions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] to the closed subgroup $B\subseteq G$, obtaining $q:G\to X$. Its statement supplies coset fibres on every test scheme and fpqc-local lifts. Since $G$ is smooth connected affine of finite type and $B$ is smooth connected and maximal solvable, [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry] applies: $X$ is a smooth geometrically integral proper separated finite-type $k$-scheme. In particular $X$ is nonempty, reduced, connected and quasi-compact. Write $p:X_R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and let $x_0=q(1)\in X(k)$; its scalar extension is a section $s:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X_R$.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358, X=G/B; Theorem 5.28, p.105; Theorem 17.9, p.354.

proof.text: Define the $R$-morphism $\delta:G_R\to H_R$ by multiplication and inversion, $\delta(g)=f_1(g)f_2(g)^{-1}$. For every $R$-scheme $T$ and $g\in G_R(T), b\in B_R(T)$, the common restriction gives $f_1(b)=f_2(b)$, and the group identities give $$\delta(gb)=f_1(g)f_1(b)f_2(b)^{-1}f_2(g)^{-1}=\delta(g).$$ Thus $\delta$ is right $B_R$-invariant as a scheme morphism, since the calculation holds on all test schemes. No commutativity of $H$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358, the coset-invariant difference morphism.

proof.text: The quotient statement [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] gives the following descent explicitly. For any $R$-scheme $T$ and $x:T\to X_R$, regard $x$ as a $k$-map to $X$ and choose its fpqc-local lifts $g_i:T_i\to G$. Pairing $g_i$ with $T_i\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ makes them $R$-maps to $G_R$. On an overlap $T_i\times_T T_j$, the coset-fibre clause gives $b_{ij}=g_i^{-1}g_j\in B(T_i\times_T T_j)$, so step 2 gives $\delta(g_i)=\delta(g_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] these maps glue uniquely to $d_T(x):T\to H_R$. Their composites to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ agree with the structure map locally and hence globally by the uniqueness clause of the same descent statement, so $d_T(x)$ is over $R$. Comparing any two lift covers on their overlaps proves independence of choices; pulling a lift cover back proves naturality in $T$, again by uniqueness. Hence Yoneda gives an $R$-morphism $d:X_R\to H_R$ with $d q_R=\delta$. Here Yoneda is simply evaluation on the universal point of $X_R$: $d=d_{X_R}(1_{X_R})$.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358, general-R functor descent; fpqc gluing: Stacks Tag 023Q, descent.tex, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms.

proof.text: The one-component case of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product] gives the canonical isomorphism $k\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. It applies because $k$ is algebraically closed and $X$ is nonempty proper reduced connected. The map $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field], including when $R$ has nilpotents. Apply [lem-pc-flat-cohomology-separated] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $M=\mathcal O_X$, $S=R$ and degree zero. Its compactness and separation hypotheses follow from step 1, and the structure sheaf is quasi-coherent. Degree-zero cohomology is global sections, with its canonical identification [lem-sc-open-cohomology-zero-sections]. The comparison formula of [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison] therefore gives the bijection $$R\otimes_k\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\longrightarrow\Gamma(X_R,\mathcal O_{X_R}),\qquad r\otimes a\longmapsto r\,a|_{X_R}.$$ On pure tensors this preserves multiplication and unit, so it is a ring isomorphism. Composing with $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ proves that the actual structure map $p^\sharp:R\to\Gamma(X_R,\mathcal O_{X_R})$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358, global sections after scalar extension; Stacks Tag 0BUG, varieties.tex, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections; Tag 02KH, coherent.tex, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, degree zero.

proof.text: As $H$ is affine, write $H=\operatorname{Spec}A$; by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] applied to $k\to A$ and $k\to R$, $H_R=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}R\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_k R)=\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_k A)$, with the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ given by $r\mapsto 1\otimes r$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] for the target $H_R$. The morphism $d$ corresponds to an $R$-algebra map $$d^\sharp:R\otimes_k A\longrightarrow\Gamma(X_R,\mathcal O_{X_R}).$$ Set $c^\sharp=(p^\sharp)^{-1}d^\sharp$. The same affine-target bijection gives an $R$-map $c:\operatorname{Spec}R\to H_R$. Since $(cp)^\sharp=p^\sharp c^\sharp=d^\sharp$, its injectivity proves $d=cp$. In particular this is equality of scheme morphisms over an arbitrary $R$, rather than only equality on geometric points.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358, affineness of the target; Stacks Tag 01I1, schemes.tex, lemma-morphism-into-affine.

proof.text: Evaluate along the section $s=q_R1_{G_R}$. Since group homomorphisms preserve the identity, $$c=ds=\delta1_{G_R}=1_{H_R}.$$ Thus $\delta=dq_R$ is the constant identity morphism. For every $R$-scheme $T$ and $g\in G_R(T)$, $f_1(g)f_2(g)^{-1}=1$ gives $f_1(g)=f_2(g)$. Evaluating this natural equality on the universal point of $G_R$ proves $f_1=f_2$. If $R$ is the zero ring, all the scalar-extended schemes are empty and the asserted equality holds uniquely as well.
